However, its insertion depth and survival time are constrained by the sustained pressure from the large-scale plasma edge during the implosion process. Our whole-process simulations demonstrated that, in the double-cone ignition scheme, the head-on collision of two deuterium-tritium plasma jets not only forms a high-density plateau with a small-scale edge, but also substantially reduces the interaction time between the heating cone and the colliding plasma to approximately 0.1 ns . This shortened interaction time enables the heating cone to remain intact after the peak compression, even when placed directly at the small-scale edge of the colliding plasma. The small-scale edge is compatible with the range of the soft-spectrum REB generated by the heating lasers. Such a REB efficiently heats a localized end-on hot spot adjacent to the high-density plateau, guided by a kT-level magnetic field amplified from a seed field during the collision process. Ignited by the localized hot spot, the high-density plateau can undergo sufficient burning and achieve a fusion energy gain of 6.8 using 60 kJ heating lasers.

articles_hidden.title: Small reconstructed brain differences may still have evolutionary relevance
articles_hidden.authors: Takanori Kochiyama, Naomichi Ogihara, Hiroki C. Tanabe, Norihiro Sadato, Takeru Akazawa

articles_hidden.title: Niche constraints drive differences between mycorrhizal fungal guilds in future range shifts
articles_hidden.authors: Joseph D. Edwards, Johan van den Hoogen, Christine V. Hawkes, Mark A. Anthony, Camille S. Delavaux, Justin D. Stewart, Kathleen K. Treseder, Xiao Feng, Monica Papeş, Robert Muscarella, Petr Baldrian, Petr Kohout, E. Toby Kiers, Thomas C. Lauber, Patrick B. Matheny, Thomas W. Crowther, Michael E. Van Nuland, Clara Qin, Colin Averill, Stephanie N. Kivlin
articles_hidden.abstract: Mycorrhizal fungi are a diverse and ubiquitous group of plant symbionts whose distribution strongly influences ecosystem function across the globe. Yet, until now, we do not have quantitative data on the range sizes of different mycorrhizal fungal taxa, limiting our capacity to forecast future shifts in community composition and function. Here, we use 115,924 DNA sequence-derived observations to map the distribution of 651 common mycorrhizal fungal taxa and forecast future changes to their range sizes. We demonstrate that climate, plant cover, and soil factors, particularly mean annual temperature, net primary productivity, and soil organic carbon, exert major control over mycorrhizal fungal distributions. Based on these drivers, the ecological niches of mycorrhizal fungi consistently differ between arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal functional guilds. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal taxa generally occupy a wider niche breadth than ectomycorrhizal fungi, occurring across larger ranges of climate, soil, plant cover, topography, and disturbance conditions. Our models also predict widespread decreases in the suitable range size of mycorrhizal fungal taxa under projected future global climates, with average ranges decreasing by 13.8% or ~2.2 million km 2 under high emissions scenarios (ssp5-8.5). This decrease in projected range size will be most pronounced for ectomycorrhizal fungi, strongly linked to constraints from their smaller overall niches. By generating a global atlas of common mycorrhizal fungi and their associated environmental niche, we establish a critical baseline for widely suspected declines in global fungal biodiversity.

articles_hidden.title: Acetate–FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis
articles_hidden.authors: Sarah de Oliveira, José Luís Fachi, Mariane Font Fernandes, Nathalia Araujo Hall, Tihana Trsan, Helder Carvalho de Assis, Arilson Bernardo dos Santos Pereira Gomes, Ana Júlia Sampaio De Sousa, André Luiz Amorim da Costa, Valquíria Aparecida Matheus, Tahila Andrighetti, Beatriz Burger, Pollyana Ribeiro Castro, Laís Passariello Pral, Bruna Toledo Nunes Pereira, Vinícius Dias Nirello, Maria Eduarda dos Santos Celeghini, Siyan Cao, Krzysztof L. Hyrc, Brian T. Layden, Susan Gilfillan, Marco Colonna, Marco Aurélio Ramirez Vinolo
articles_hidden.abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are required for the protective effects of acetate, which are also dependent on FFAR2 signaling and IL-22. Neutrophil-specific deletion of FFAR2 impairs IL-22 responses, increases epithelial damage, and exacerbates colitis, while administration of recombinant IL-22 is sufficient to restore acetate protection in this context. Analysis of human ulcerative colitis biopsies reveals increased FFAR2 + neutrophils correlating with IL-22-related gene signatures. These findings indicate that acetate–FFAR2–neutrophil–IL-22 axis modulates intestinal inflammation, revealing a metabolic mechanism that links microbiota-derived signals to mucosal protection and highlighting potential therapeutic targets for inflammatory bowel diseases.

articles_hidden.title: A genome-wide senescence synthetic lethality screen identifies PARP16 as a senolytic target
articles_hidden.authors: Shohini Ghosh-Choudhary, Jie Liu, Delphine Beaulieu, Ricardo Pineda, Haoxiang Yang, Shria Moturi, Mads B. Larsen, Irene Alfaras, Mehdi Pirooznia, Shihui Liu, Jonathan K. Alder, Yuan Liu, Bill B. Chen, Melanie Königshoff, Toren Finkel
articles_hidden.abstract: Accumulation of senescent cells is increasingly viewed as a significant contributor to aging and age-related diseases. To date, the elimination of senescent cells through small molecule senolytic agents has largely relied on a limited number of repurposed agents, often leveraged from previous oncological applications. Here, we describe a CRISPR-based, genome-wide, synthetic lethal screen for senescent cells. From this screen, we identify a number of genes whose deletion appears to be well tolerated in normal proliferating cells, but whose deletion is lethal in the context of senescence. We further characterize one promising candidate gene encoding the ER-resident protein PARP16. Knockdown of PARP16 does not affect the viability of mouse or human cells but results in the death of a wide range of senescent cells. Furthermore, two distinct small molecule PARP16 inhibitors have little effect of normal cell growth but result in the selective death of senescent cells in culture and in freshly isolated human donor lung tissue explants. Together, these results demonstrate a rational strategy to identify novel senolytic therapies that could have potential applications for a wide range of age-related conditions.

articles_hidden.title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause
articles_hidden.authors: Stephanie M. Perez, Angela M. Boley, Hannah B. Reiley, Olivia J. Yang, Kayla Lilly, Daniel J. Lodge
articles_hidden.abstract: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman’s lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing “estrogen protection hypothesis,” which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield inconsistent results. Our results establish that perimenopause is a mechanistically distinct neurobiological window characterized by a unique failure of hippocampal-dopamine circuit regulation. By identifying this specific period of circuit instability, this work provides a framework for stage-specific psychiatric interventions and reframes reproductive aging as a series of distinct transitions in brain function.

articles_hidden.title: Competitive disruption of COI1 receptor assembly by a hemibiotrophic bacterial effector suppresses jasmonate-mediated immunity
articles_hidden.authors: Peng Cao, Yuyan An, Xinjing Li, Jiaoru Zhao, Xi Zhang, Wen Li, Yanling Gan, Jun Liu, Meixiang Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Hormone pathways are central hubs in plant immunity, and their receptors, the critical initiators of signaling cascades, are logical targets of pathogen effectors. The jasmonic acid (JA) pathway is a cornerstone of defense against phytopathogens, especially necrotrophs. However, whether pathogens can directly target its receptor COI1 to subvert this defense layer has remained unclear. Here, we show that JA signaling positively regulates resistance to the devastating hemibiotrophic pathogen Ralstonia solanacearum and identified a bacterial effector, RipBO, that directly targets COI1 to counteract this defense. RipBO binds with high affinity to the F-box domain of COI1, competitively disrupts the COI1-ASK interaction, and thereby blocks SCF COI1 complex assembly. This disruption effectively stabilizes JAZ repressors and paralyzes JA-mediated immunity. Our findings clarify the contribution of JA signaling to bacterial wilt resistance and identify direct targeting of the hormone receptor as a pathogen virulence strategy, pointing to a potential vulnerability for crop protection.

articles_hidden.title: Language model teams as distributed systems
articles_hidden.authors: Elizabeth Mieczkowski, Katherine M. Collins, Ilia Sucholutsky, Natalia Vélez, Thomas L. Griffiths
articles_hidden.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are growing increasingly powerful. Yet, fundamental constraints on the reasoning, memory, and performance of individual models has sparked recent interest in scaling abilities using LLM teams. With growing deployment of LLM teams at scale, there is a need for principled guidelines for when teams help, how many agents to use, and how structure impacts performance. Rather than building these teams through trial-and-error, we propose using distributed systems as a formal foundation for designing and evaluating LLM teams. Under this formal framework, we derive predictions about how task structure and team architecture should shape performance. Empirical evidence supports these predictions: LLM team scaling follows classical distributed computing laws based on the structure of a task, and centralized and decentralized architectures exhibit the asymmetric vulnerabilities predicted by distributed systems theory. These results establish distributed computing as a generative framework that yields testable, quantitative predictions about LLM team behavior and informs the construction of more efficient and capable teams.

articles_hidden.title: Overlooked biodiversity hotspots revealed by a pluralistic approach for quantifying amphibian biodiscovery needs
articles_hidden.authors: Sky T. Button, Amaël Borzée
articles_hidden.abstract: Undocumented and poorly known species spanning Linnean and Wallacean biodiversity shortfalls pose a major challenge to conservation due to the uncertainty they introduce. To address this, we developed a novel pluralistic approach that accounts for sampling gaps, spatial patterns, environmental associations, and varying conservation needs simultaneously, using amphibians as a case study. Using environment-based richness models and species accumulation curves (SACs), we identified areas with high biodiscovery needs for amphibians. These were concentrated primarily in humid tropical South America, sub-Saharan Africa, and East/Southeast Asia. While environmental models produced more reliable richness estimates than SACs overall, SAC-based estimates nonetheless added unique insights, especially in biodiverse, moderately well-sampled areas like Costa Rica and Panama. By integrating environmental models and SACs—thus leveraging combined strengths of previous approaches—our holistic scoring technique also proved consistent in estimating biodiscovery priorities across ecoregions, enabling robust recommendations for future sampling.

articles_hidden.title: The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
articles_hidden.authors: Anne Boyeldieu, Mathilde Vallette, Mathieu Bergé, Clarisse Roblin, Lama Shamseddine, Anna M. Diaz-Rovira, Anne-Lise Soulet, Christian Basset, Lauriane Plouhinec, Agnès Amouric, Salomé Milhavet, Léa Mélissa Perrault, Joana Marx Pereira da Cunha, Calum Johnston, Sylvie Kieffer-Jaquinod, Marc Maresca, Josette Perrier, Anne Chouquet, Cécile Morlot, Victor Guallar, Michael Lafond, Victor Duarte, Nathalie Campo, Patrice Polard
articles_hidden.abstract: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI c 1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI c 1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.

articles_hidden.title: Leptin Receptor + cells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14
articles_hidden.authors: Yuanyuan Xue, Ruixuan Zhang, Maowu Luo, Amanda R. Reyes, Salma Merchant, Trevor S. Tippetts, Gerik Grabowski, Tai Ngo, Yanan Sophia Zhang, Zhiguo Shang, Nisi Jiang, Nathaniel S. Tjahjono, Elise C. Jeffery, Yafeng Li, Tao Wei, Wen Gu, Liming Du, Ralph J. DeBerardinis, Kevin M. Dean, David W. Schmidtke, Thomas P. Mathews, Daniel Lucas, Zhiyu Zhao, Sean J. Morrison
articles_hidden.abstract: Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR + ) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepR + cells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14. Cxcl14 -expressing LepR + cells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion of Cxcl14 from LepR + cells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes from Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice expressed lower levels of genes that encode granule proteins as compared to control mice, leading to the release of platelets with fewer α-granules and defective thrombus formation/growth. CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, in Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice. CXCL14 protein was sufficient to promote platelet formation by megakaryocytes in vitro and in vivo. LepR + cells thus create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis by producing CXCL14, which regulates lipid metabolism and terminal differentiation in megakaryocytes.

articles_hidden.title: Local interactions drive hyperuniform tissue coverage during development
articles_hidden.authors: Sandra Siegert, Lida Kanari, Mehmet Can Uçar
articles_hidden.abstract: In living tissues, branched cells must efficiently cover territories to perform essential functions ranging from neural signaling to immune surveillance. However, how cells collectively establish and optimize tissue-scale coverage without global regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a biophysical theory of interacting branched cells and show that coupling their growth to neighbor repulsion drives efficient tissue tiling with minimal territorial overlap. Strikingly, our model predicts that the same local mechanism progressively suppresses long-range density fluctuations during development, driving the system toward a large-scale order called hyperuniformity. We confirm these theoretical predictions on microglial patterning in the developing retina and show that in perturbation experiments with limited arbor growth, both tiling and fluctuation suppression are disrupted. Our results reveal that two seemingly distinct features of tissue organization, efficient space-filling and large-scale order, share a single dynamical origin, suggesting a general principle for robust tissue patterning.

articles_hidden.title: Knowledge gaps and scientific progress
articles_hidden.authors: Kara Kedrick, Wenlong Yang, Thomas Gebhart, Yang Wang, Russell J. Funk
articles_hidden.abstract: Knowledge production is often viewed as an endogenous process in which discovery arises through the recombination of existing theories, findings, and concepts. Yet not all recombinations are equally valuable, and identifying those that may prove most generative remains challenging. We propose that a crucial form of recombination occurs when linking concepts creates knowledge gaps—empty regions in the conceptual landscape that may focus scientific attention on unexplored connections. Using computational topology, we develop a method to identify knowledge gaps in science at scale. In this framework, gaps form when new connections complete cycles in evolving networks of scientific concepts. We apply the method to 34,363,623 papers in Microsoft Academic Graph spanning 1900 to 2020. The main analyses use samples ranging from 8,643,571 to 31,983,201 papers. Compared with papers that introduce novel concept pairs without opening gaps, gap-opening papers have greater long-term citation impact, are more disruptive of prior work, and exhibit greater delayed recognition. Gap-opening papers receive fewer citations within five years of publication but more over twenty years, consistent with scientific communities needing time to recognize and develop newly opened research territories. Evidence for the generative capacity of gap-opening papers—as indicated by high citation impact and disruption—replicates in five additional databases (OpenAlex, the PubMed Knowledge Graph, Dimensions, American Physical Society journals, and United States patents) and across eight concept vocabularies, including several derived directly from text. Together, these results point to a distinctive generative role for gap opening in scientific discovery.

articles_hidden.title: A decadal record of isotopic trends in martian atmospheric CO 2
articles_hidden.authors: Heather B. Franz, Christopher R. Webster, Gregory J. Flesch, Paul R. Mahaffy, Eric Raaen, Melinda Kahre, Benito Prats, Bethany L. Ehlmann, Sushil K. Atreya, David G. Burtt, Christopher H. House, Daniel Y. Lo, Jennifer C. Stern, Melissa G. Trainer, P. Douglas Archer, Manuel de la Torre Juarez, Scott Guzewich, German M. Martinez, Charles A. Malespin, Jorge Pla-Garcia, Scot C. R. Rafkin, Andrew Steele, Ashwin R. Vasavada, Daniel Víudez-Moreiras, Michael H. Wong, Maria-Paz Zorzano
articles_hidden.abstract: This work represents the first long-term record of the isotopic composition of martian atmospheric CO 2 , acquired in situ by the Curiosity rover at Gale crater during Mars Years (MY) 31–38 (2012–2025). Measurement campaigns were designed to investigate possibilities of both diurnal and seasonal effects on CO 2 isotopes. Coordinated pairs of analyses during MY 31 and 38 revealed no significant differences in isotopic composition of CO 2 acquired during daytime and nighttime hours. However, here we show evidence for modest enrichment in heavy isotopes of oxygen in both northern and southern hemisphere spring-summer seasons. We assessed several processes, including precipitation/sublimation and adsorption/desorption of CO 2 , CO 2 photolysis, and oxygen isotope exchange as potential candidates for producing the observed fractionations. We find that while sublimation of CO 2 from polar caps, sublimation and desorption of CO 2 from lower latitude reservoirs, and CO 2 photolysis are insufficient alone, we can reproduce the measured enrichment through modeling of isotope exchange between CO 2 and 18 O-enriched H 2 O in thin liquid-like films at Mars’ surface or adsorbed within the regolith as Mars approaches and transits through perihelion. Lesser 18 O enrichment near aphelion may reflect less favorable conditions for oxygen isotope exchange at lower temperatures. Observed seasonal variations in CO 2 carbon isotopic composition are less pronounced, consistent with less carbon isotope exchange with surface reservoirs than seen for oxygen. Since our measurements were obtained at a single near-equatorial location on Mars, the relative contributions from global, regional, and local processes cannot be well-constrained by the available data.

articles_hidden.title: China’s energy transition strategy favoring both coal and renewables: Economic risks and global implications
articles_hidden.authors: Xiaoli Zhang, Xueqin Cui, Daniel M. Kammen
articles_hidden.abstract: China’s energy strategy is navigating a complex policy landscape: While leading the world in renewable energy manufacturing and deployment, it is simultaneously pursuing a continued expansion of its coal-fired power fleet. This paper examines this dual trajectory by building an integrated analytical framework that combines domestic and international perspectives to analyze the social, economic, climate, and geopolitical impacts of China’s new coal-power plant investments. Combining historical trends, government planning, and projections from influential policy teams, we find that a tripling of renewable capacity by 2030, a pace China is on track to meet, is sufficient to satisfy all projected electricity demand scenarios when considered alongside the evolving generation mix and planned storage deployment. We further show that additional coal capacity is not required to ensure adequate electricity supply under these scenarios. The coal pathway could expose up to $223.6 billion of stranded assets from new projects and add an additional 327,000 workers in a declining industry. Furthermore, this trajectory may weaken the alignment between China’s domestic energy investment and its international clean energy leadership. We conclude that a clean-energy-led pathway that halts new coal construction is lower-cost, better for job growth, and more consistent with China’s role as a leader in the global clean energy transition.

articles_hidden.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
articles_hidden.authors: Fan Zhang, Sota Takagi, Kouhei Ichiyanagi, Liang Xu, Yue Wu, Zezhou Li, Yuan Tian, Jichen Xu, Qingjin Zeng, Shipan Yin, Yang Liu, Nobuaki Kawai, Hiroaki Kishimura, Kohei Miyanishi, Keiichi Sueda, Tadashi Togashi, Hirotaka Nakamura, Norimasa Ozaki, Alexis Amouretti, Toshinori Yabuuchi, Lin Wang, Hongnian Cai, Hongwei Sheng, Xingwang Cheng, Mingwei Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC–HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC–HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure–temperature ( P-T ) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC–HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock P-T state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme P-T conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast, reversible transformations.

articles_hidden.title: Neurovascular protein half-lives in health and aging
articles_hidden.authors: Benjamin D. Gastfriend, Lucija Pintarić, Irfan Baig, David J. Gonzalez, Richard Daneman
articles_hidden.abstract: Specializations of blood vasculature in the central nervous system (CNS), including the blood–brain barrier (BBB), neurovascular coupling, and perivascular spaces, maintain CNS homeostasis and become dysfunctional in disease and aging. Protein turnover, the process by which proteins are continually degraded and replaced, profoundly influences cell and tissue function and is dysregulated in aging and disease. Understanding the turnover of neurovascular proteins could provide insight into how the vasculature achieves both long-term structural stability and dynamic regulation. Vascular proteins, however, are underrepresented in previous studies of in vivo brain protein turnover. In this work, we used stable isotope labeling, nonenzymatic blood vessel enrichment, and high-resolution mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify the half-lives of brain vascular proteins in young adult and aged mice. We report half-life estimates for 1,358 proteins, including components of endothelial junctions, BBB transporters, astrocyte endfoot proteins, and vascular basement membrane proteins. We found that certain classes of proteins with related functions had similar half-lives, including BBB junctional proteins (~3 d), BBB transporters (~2 to 6 d), and most basement membrane components (>30 d). We also identified peptide motifs enriched in proteins with short and long half-lives and found differences in half-life distributions for cell type–specific proteomes. Finally, although we did not observe a global age-related shift in vascular protein turnover, we did identify specific proteins with increased or decreased half-lives in aging. This work establishes a high-quality database of neurovascular protein half-lives and provides a foundation for understanding how protein turnover contributes to neurovascular function and age-associated dysfunction.

articles_hidden.title: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants
articles_hidden.authors: Jonathan Z. Shik, Mads Ditlevsen, Anke J. Posma, Aoife O’Brien, Katrine Skjold Ottesen, Olivia-Sofie Basse Schougaard, Rasmus Stenbak Larsen, Asta Rødsgaard-Jørgensen, Anders Michelsen, Riikka Rinnan, Juliano Morimoto
articles_hidden.abstract: Maintaining optimized nutrient exchange between partnered species across changing environments presents a fundamental challenge for nutritional mutualisms. Yet quantitative approaches linking nutrient acquisition by one partner with the nutritional requirements of the other have been lacking. Here we extend the Nutritional Geometry Framework from organisms and colonies to interspecific mutualisms by linking realized nutritional niches (RNNs) with nutritional performance landscapes to quantify nutritional homeostasis between interacting species. Nutritional analyses of thousands of DNA-barcoded plant fragments collected by free-ranging Panamanian leafcutter ants revealed that RNNs for fungal cultivar provisioning diverged between degraded urban and intact rainforest habitats. Despite this, colonies converged on similar nutritional intake targets that were similarly positioned relative to regions of high fungal performance, while fungal nutritional yield remained stable across habitats. These findings demonstrate that correspondence between colony nutritional intake and fungal nutritional performance provides a quantitative means of assessing nutritional homeostasis across interacting species and establishes a foundation for comparative analyses of nutrient exchange across mutualisms experiencing environmental change.

articles_hidden.title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
articles_hidden.authors: Ke Zhang, Yaoyao Han, Lindsey Gillson, Xiaoling Zhang, Suzanne McGowan, Michael E. Meadows, Yuan Jin, Luki Subehi, John A. Dearing, David P. Hamilton, Yan Zhao, Lian Pin Koh, David Taylor
articles_hidden.abstract: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth’s surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

articles_hidden.title: Lipid-induced Caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking is associated with lipid droplet growth
articles_hidden.authors: Esther Ocket, Tamara Pietrucik, Luis Wong-Dilworth, Daniel Aik, Michaela Rath, Dmytro Puchkov, Max Ruwolt, Martin Lehmann, Claudia Matthaeus
articles_hidden.abstract: Caveolae are 50 to 100 nm sized plasma membrane invaginations involved in cellular lipid uptake and lipid accumulation. Several caveolin1 and cavin1 mutations are associated with human lipodystrophy. Previous research identified caveolae proteins at lipid droplets, although their specific cellular function at lipid droplets is not understood. Here, we show that extracellular dietary lipids like oleic acid and cholesterol shift caveolae at the plasma membrane to highly spherical invaginations and induce the internalization of caveolin1. Within 3 h of lipid treatment, caveolin1 accumulates specifically to lipid droplets. Correlative fluorescence Focused Ion Beam – Scanning Electron Microscopy and split-APEX proteomics revealed that this localization occurs in the absence of intact caveolar vesicles but caveolin1 alone. Mechanistically, caveolin1 trafficking to lipid droplets is regulated by EHD2 at the plasma membrane, is dynamin independent, and proceeds via EEA1- and Rab5-positive endosomes within 1 h of oleic acid treatment. Lipid droplet accumulation of caveolin1 is independent of lysosomal activity. Functionally, caveolin1-enriched lipid droplets exhibit a significant increase in size, demonstrating that caveolin1 is critical for lipid droplet growth. Notably, the deletion of the central caveolin1 β-barrel (Cav1-F160X), a mutation identified in lipodystrophy patients, abolished caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking and lipid droplet growth. Taken together, our results show that dietary lipids trigger caveolin1 internalization and accumulation at lipid droplets and a caveolin1-dependent lipid droplet growth, thereby providing an initial mechanistic basis for the lipodystrophic phenotype associated with caveolin1 mutations.

articles_hidden.title: Harness design matters for AI capabilities in mathematics
articles_hidden.authors: Mohammed Abouzaid, Nikhil Srivastava, Rachel Ward, Lauren Williams
articles_hidden.abstract: To assess the ability of current AI systems to correctly solve research-level mathematics problems, we tested four AI systems on a set of ten problems in a broad range of mathematical fields; these problems arose naturally in the research process of the contributors. This document includes our methodology, and the results of our testing, including the assessment of human reviewers and a report of costs. We provide links to supplementary documents including the human solutions, the AI-generated solutions, and the referee reports and logs for the AI-generated solutions.

articles_hidden.title: Anomeric configuration encodes mesophase preference of glucosylceramides in phospholipid membranes
articles_hidden.authors: Shayak Biswas, Rajendra Rohokale, Sayan Kundu, Mingwei Zhou, Md. Shamiul Islam, Jiatong Guo, Rajendra Mane, Selena Dessain, Gail E. Fanucci, Zhongwu Guo
articles_hidden.abstract: Glycosphingolipids are key components of the cell glycocalyx, yet the extent to which their anomeric configuration affects their membrane organization remains unclear. Glucosylceramide (GlcCer) exists as α- and β-anomers with distinct biological activities, while the biophysical basis for these differences is unknown. Here, using nitroxide spin-labeled analogs of α- and β-GlcCer, we examined how the glycosidic stereochemistry affects their partitioning in phospholipid bilayers. In 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine, dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine, and distearoylphosphatidylcholine liposomes, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra of both probes contained two components: a broad, motion-restricted component consistent with GlcCer incorporated into the lamellar lipid bilayer and a sharp, highly mobile component attributed to some segregated, bilayer-associated GlcCer-rich nano-assemblies. EPR spectral simulations and complementary analyses showed that α-GlcCer predominantly partitioned into the lamellar phospholipid phase, whereas β-GlcCer was strongly enriched in the segregated GlcCer-rich phase. Importantly, analogous anomer-dependent EPR behavior was also observed for aqueous GlcCer dispersions in the absence of phospholipids, indicating that the distinct assembly propensities are intrinsic to the glycolipids and are modulated, rather than created, by the phospholipids. These findings support a two-mesophase model in which anomeric configuration acts as a stereochemical switch that biases GlcCer between phospholipid lamellae and segregated glycolipid nano-assemblies. Notably, such anomer-dependent behaviors were observed at a probe loading of only 0.5 mol%. Thus, even at rather low abundance, a subtle stereochemical difference in GlcCer can substantially alter its compatibility with a phospholipid membrane matrix, providing a plausible physical basis for anomer-dependent glycolipid sorting, signaling, and disease-associated membrane organization.

articles_hidden.title: Reply to Kochiyama et al.: Extensive inferred overlap in cognitive abilities complicate evolutionary models of Neanderthal replacement
articles_hidden.authors: P. Thomas Schoenemann, Jia-Hong Gao, Guoyuan Yang

articles_hidden.title: Anthropocentric comparisons with human language impede our understanding of whale communication
articles_hidden.authors: Luke Rendell, Laela S. Sayigh, Vincent M. Janik, Frants H. Jensen, Stephanie L. King, Peter T. Madsen, Peter L. Tyack

articles_hidden.title: Basal radial glia abundance and morphotype diversity in the hippocampal dentate gyrus imply their evolutionarily ancient origin
articles_hidden.authors: Matilde Aquilino, Nikola Cokorac, Liliia Andriichuk, Emanuele Capra, Kana Shimazu, Leena Ivancic, Chiara Ossola, Vasiliki Gkini, Shinobu Goto, Masato Sawada, Kazuya Kuboyama, Yasuhiko Ozaki, Mayumi Sugiura-Ogasawara, Kazunobu Sawamoto, Nereo Kalebic, Takashi Namba
articles_hidden.abstract: Basal radial glia (bRG) are neural progenitor cells (NPCs) essential for primate neocortical expansion, but their presence in other brain regions and across species remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the developing mouse dentate gyrus (DG), unlike the neocortex, harbors abundant NPCs that transcriptionally and morphologically resemble human neocortical bRG. This striking abundance is conserved across other Boreoeutherian species, including mice, marmosets, ferrets, and pigs. Comparative transcriptomics uncovered a shared morphoregulatory gene signature between bRG in mouse DG and human neocortex. Immunohistochemical analysis showed diversity in DG bRG morphotypes across species. Remarkably, compared to the neocortex, DG bRG consistently exhibit greater morphotype diversity. Ancestral state reconstruction suggests that this diversity was already present in the common ancestor of Boreoeutherians. Together, our findings position the DG as a conserved, evolutionarily ancient niche for bRG, revealing that region- and species-specific adaptations of NPCs extend beyond the neocortex.

articles_hidden.title: Unconventional modulation of Na v 1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain
articles_hidden.authors: Xi Zhou, Huan Wang, Minjuan Lu, Ye Cong, Jiangtao Zhang, Minzhi Chen, Jialing Cai, Jichen Zhang, Qihang Liu, Junhao Huang, Nieng Yan, Xueqin Jin, Zhonghua Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium (Na v ) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Na v channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from Lychas mucronatus . LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Na v 1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNa v 1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSD II ) and the extracellular loop III (ECL III ) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3–S4 II loop and displaces S0/S3 II helices to trap VSD II within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSD II conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSD II trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECL III engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECL III region underlie the prominent species- and isoform-dependent activities of the toxin toward insect and mammalian Na v channels. Our study provides a structural basis for the dual-action mechanisms of β-scorpion toxins on Na v channels and presents a structural framework for understanding toxin binding, channel gating modulation, ecological adaptation, and rational drug design.

articles_hidden.title: Direct CO 2 splitting using light-based catalysis and an oxygen reservoir
articles_hidden.authors: Shan Z. Deneen, Catherine J. Fabiano, Alexander Ahrens, Matheus Laureano Nunes Barbosa, Luke Kay, Andrés B. Sánchez-Alvarado, Nolan Craft, Peter Nordlander, Naomi J. Halas
articles_hidden.abstract: As the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, the conversion of CO 2 into value-added products is vital for achieving a circular economy. CO 2 activation typically requires coreactants, high temperatures, or significant electrical input, any of which increases cost or limits scalability. Here we demonstrate a straightforward way to split CO 2 directly into carbon monoxide and oxygen using light. By combining a light-driven antenna-reactor photocatalyst with a material that acts as an oxygen reservoir, CO 2 can be decomposed directly into CO and oxygen with light only. Under illumination, photoexcited carriers induce CO 2 bond dissociation, while cerium oxide adsorbs the released oxygen into vacancy sites, preventing recombination. The oxygen can then be released from the ceria by flowing nitrogen under white light illumination, a process that can be repeated multiple times, restoring full photocatalytic activity. This demonstrates a practical and scalable strategy for efficient CO 2 conversion, shifting the chemical equilibrium of CO 2 dissociation in a controllable manner.

articles_hidden.title: Chaperone modulation and the structural basis for sRNA recognition by the conserved ribonuclease YicC
articles_hidden.authors: Kai Katsuya-Gaviria, Giulia Paris, Ben F. Luisi, Aleksei Lulla
articles_hidden.abstract: The broadly conserved bacterial endoribonuclease YicC represents a widespread but enigmatic family of RNA processing enzymes with poorly defined substrate selectivity. Here, we show that Escherichia coli YicC displays a distinct selectivity, cleaving small regulatory RNAs (sRNAs) such as RyhB and RprA but not when they are in complexes with cognate mRNA targets or RNA sponges. Furthermore, we demonstrate that RyhB processing is modulated, but not abolished, by the RNA chaperone Hfq. Our cryo-EM structures of E. coli YicC in apo form and in complexes with substrate and nonsubstrate RNA species capture marked quaternary and tertiary structural switches triggered by sRNA stem-loop binding that engulf and ratchet the RNA into an internal catalytic channel. Structural comparison of cleavable (RyhB) and noncleavable (MicA) sRNA-bound complexes reveal a near-identical ground-state binding mode, proving that cavity docking is sequence-tolerant and decoupled from catalytic execution. Together, our findings suggest that YicC may be a state-selective endoribonuclease and reveal a framework for selective RNA clearance in bacterial posttranscriptional regulation.

articles_hidden.title: Structural basis for the selective inhibition of the PI3KC3-C2 complex by Rubicon in endolysosome maturation and mitophagy
articles_hidden.authors: Minghao Chen, Aniketh Bishnu, Yongjia Duan, Julia F. Riley, Qingyang Ni, Aaron M. N. Joiner, Isaac J. Allen, Erika L. F. Holzbaur, Ian G. Ganley, James H. Hurley
articles_hidden.abstract: Rubicon is a negative regulator of autophagy and the endolysosomal network (ELN) and an antagonist of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex II (PI3KC3-C2). Inhibition of Rubicon is considered a potential means to therapeutically upregulate autophagy and the ELN to treat Parkinson’s disease and other conditions characterized by autophagic and ELN dysfunction. Rubicon is specific for the UV radiation resistance-associated gene protein (UVRAG)-containing PI3KC3-C2 over the purely autophagic ATG14-containing PI3KC3-C1 complex. Here, we determined the high-resolution cryoelectron microscopy structure of PI3KC3-C2 in complex with the PI3KC3-binding domain of Rubicon and compared it to cryo-EM structures of unbound PI3KC3-C2 and PI3KC3-C1. Rubicon binds directly to PI3KC3-C2 only via the BARA domain of the BECN1 subunit, which is common to both C1 and C2. The selectivity of Rubicon for the PI3KC3-C2 complex over the PI3KC3-C1 complex is attributed to a conformation of the BECN1 BARA domain induced by UVRAG, rather than to direct contact with UVRAG or direct antagonism by the ATG14 subunit of PI3KC3-C1. Targeted disruption of the Rubicon:PI3K3-C2 structural interface by site-directed mutations enhances mitophagic activity in human epithelial cells to levels comparable to those observed in Rubicon knockout cells. Similarly, disruption of the interaction in Rubicon-overexpressing hippocampal neurons restored lysosomal flux to wild-type levels. These data show that suppressing the function of PI3K3-C2 can fully account for the negative regulatory effects of Rubicon in the autophagy and ELN pathways.

articles_hidden.title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing
articles_hidden.authors: Lluís Camprubí-Ferrer, Jesús Soldán-Hidalgo, Emil Axell, Marzia Dell’Eva, Marta García-Cruzado, Juan García-Revilla, Yiyi Yang, Rosalía Fernández-Calle, Logan Larlham, Bhanu Chouhan, Rocío Talaverón, Agnes Paulus, Lukas Danielson, Angela Gomez-Arboledas, Oxana Klementieva, Antonia Gutierrez, Javier Vitorica, Malin Wennström, Gunnar K. Gouras, Javier Frontiñán-Rubio, Antonio Boza-Serrano, Gabriel A. Rabinovich, José Luis Venero, Tomas Deierborg
articles_hidden.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3 + microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1 + dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like proteins, supporting a role for this lectin in immune receptor regulation. Complementary in vivo transcriptomic profiling showed that Gal3 deletion suppresses type I interferon and microglial neurodegenerative transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings position Gal3 at the interface between Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and plaque-associated microglial responses in AD.

articles_hidden.title: SCN1B intron 3 retention results in a nonsense-mediated decay–sensitive mRNA linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
articles_hidden.authors: Shreeya Bakshi, Amanda M. Catalfio, Chunling Chen, Yukun Yuan, Luis F. Lopez-Santiago, Chloe Moore, Daniel S. Seagull, Sahana Macedo, Aazif Hussein, Isha Verma, Kyle Stokes, Joe Minton, Louis T. Dang, Christelle M. El Achkar, Annapurna Poduri, Jack M. Parent, Lori L. Isom
articles_hidden.abstract: Biallelic variants in the voltage-gated sodium channel (VGSC) gene SCN1B are linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy type 52 (DEE52). SCN1B encodes two isoforms: transmembrane β1, generated by all 6 coding exons, and β1B, generated by exons 1 to 3 followed by retention of intron 3 ( SCN1B -IR). Transmembrane β1 subunits are multifunctional proteins that regulate sodium current and channel cell-surface expression, participate in cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion, and modulate transcription. Several DEE52 variants in the transmembrane β1 coding region have been shown to result in mixed loss-of-function. DEE52 variants are also identified in SCN1B -IR, yet their functional impacts remain unknown. Here, we provide evidence that SCN1B -IR is a cell type–specific, nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)–sensitive transcript. We investigate a severe biallelic DEE52 patient variant in intron 3, SCN1B c.449-2A>G, which results in expression of SCN1B -IR, but not transmembrane β1 transcripts. A transgenic mouse model that expresses SCN1B -IR, but not transmembrane β1, transcript phenocopies Scn1b null mice with seizures and early death. Thus, SCN1B -IR functions as an NMD-sensitive transcript that cannot compensate for the loss of transmembrane β1. We propose that future work may reveal SCN1B -IR to be a therapeutic target similar to other NMD-targeted transcripts.

articles_hidden.title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys
articles_hidden.authors: Bozhao Zhang, Kaihui Xun, Pengfei Guan, Robert O. Ritchie, Jun Ding
articles_hidden.abstract: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy–interstitial diffusivity convergence. We develop and validate a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential based on the moment tensor potential formalism for body-centered-cubic Zr–Ti–Nb alloys, enabling accurate large-scale simulations of defect energetics and migration. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a robust inverse correlation between LLD and the activation energy disparity between vacancies and interstitials. This relationship is further validated in face-centered-cubic V–Co–Ni and Ni–Pd systems, demonstrating transferability across distinct chemistries and crystal structures. LLD-induced narrowing of vacancy–interstitial mobility differences promotes Frenkel pair recombination and defect self-healing. Mechanistically, vacancy diffusion is governed by the energy barrier associated with bond-length compression at the saddle state, together with statistical sampling of low-barrier jumps mediated by oversized atoms. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful, physically grounded design lever that links nanoscale disorder to point-defect self-healing, offering a practical pathway for the accelerated discovery of next-generation structural materials for extreme environments.

articles_hidden.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
articles_hidden.authors: Nicolas Boullé, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend
articles_hidden.abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

articles_hidden.title: The AI scientist in the mirror: Shared flaws, joint remedies
