We reveal that the intrinsic polysulfide conversion efficiency of spinel oxides is cooperatively governed by two structural features. Further screening of promising catalysts is conducted using the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of these features on spinel oxides. The model identifies Fe 2 CoO 4 and Fe 2 NiO 4 as superior catalysts, which are experimentally validated to exhibit excellent performance. This work provides deep mechanistic insights and a powerful data-driven framework for the rational design of spinel catalysts, with potential extension to other applications.

articles_hidden.title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
articles_hidden.authors: Marco Vidal-Cordasco, Guillermo Rodríguez-Gómez, Ana B. Marín-Arroyo
articles_hidden.abstract: To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of Homo sapiens , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and H. sapiens lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of H. sapiens remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and H. sapiens dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

articles_hidden.title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
articles_hidden.authors: Yuqi Qian, Wenlei Song, James Head, Mingyu Tian, Zhuang Guo, Harald Hiesinger, Carolyn H. van der Bogert, Le Zhang, Jingyou Chen, Wanfeng Zhang, Ziqing Li, Lingzhi Sun, Xiangsong Wang, Wei-Ran Li, Jiacheng Liu, Nicolas Dauphas, Yi-Gang Xu, Guochun Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

articles_hidden.title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
articles_hidden.authors: Xiewei Xiong, Wanhui Xu, Na Li, Sichen Xing, Ziyi Huang, Jiayi Chen, Li Li, Tong Zhu, Hao Pei
articles_hidden.abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

articles_hidden.title: Platelet glycoprotein Ib shapes the immune response during lung injury
articles_hidden.authors: David Köhler, Anna Biedritzky, Philipp Burkard, Chunguang Liang, Linyan Tang, Alice Bernard, Philipp Dignus, Tim Steiner, Tiago F. Granja, Claudia Eggstein, Chao Liu, Lina M. Serna-Higuita, Diana Dudziak, Thomas Dandekar, Valbona Mirakaj, Bernhard Nieswandt, Peter Rosenberger
articles_hidden.abstract: The acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening, inflammatory disease state of the lung. Self-propagating inflammation within the alveolar space and excessive infiltration of neutrophils into the pulmonary airspace are the main mechanisms underlying the dysfunction. A role of platelets in the pathogenesis of ARDS is suggested, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. We hypothesized that platelet glycoprotein (GP)Ib is an important contributor of platelet activation in this context. To highlight the contribution of the GPIb to the acute phase of experimental ALI in mice, we exposed mice genetically lacking functional GPIb ( GPIb-IL-4tg ) and wild-type (WT) mice injected with a function blocking anti-GPIb antibody to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated mice displayed reduced neutrophil infiltration of the alveolar space in response to LPS. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated WT mice showed reduced interactions of platelets with neutrophils in comparison to controls, resulting in reduced platelet-neutrophil complexes and mitigated formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. Since these mechanisms are important for defense against external invasion of pathogens, we exposed GPIb-IL-4tg mice to Klebsiella pneumoniae and found reduced survival with increased bacterial load in these animals. Last, translational evaluation of biosamples of patients with ARDS showed that patients with low plasma levels of the shed GPIbα ectodomain (glycocalicin) exhibited higher mortality and worsened overall outcome. Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.

articles_hidden.title: SMAD4 loss drives cancer chromosomal instability through transcription-replication conflict–associated replication stress
articles_hidden.authors: Atmika Paul, Gargee Joshi, Philipp Jungk, Simranjeet Kaur, Shengyu Yao, Ioannis Tsirkas, Nicolas Böhly, Maren Sitte, Gabriela Salinas, Stephan Hamperl, Maik Kschischo, Holger Bastians
articles_hidden.abstract: Cancer chromosomal instability (CIN) drives tumor evolution through generating structural and numerical chromosome aberrations. However, its molecular determinants remain poorly characterized. Here, we uncover a yet unrecognized role for the tumor suppressor SMAD4 as a key regulator of chromosomal stability. Mechanistically, loss of SMAD4 causes replication stress by promoting transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) and induces subsequent mitotic errors, leading to the concomitant emergence of structural and numerical CIN. While the tumor suppressor function of SMAD4 has been predominantly attributed to transforming growth factor–β signaling, we find that its role in genome maintenance operates via bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and its transcriptional target gene ID3 . Consequently, inhibition of BMP signaling mimics the loss of SMAD4 , while reexpression of SMAD4 or ID3 in SMAD4 -deficient colorectal or pancreatic cancer cells suppresses TRCs, replication stress, and mitotic errors. Our findings reveal a TRC- and replication stress–driven mechanism by which loss of BMP-SMAD4 signaling causes cancer CIN.

articles_hidden.title: Self-assembly of bacterial volumetric patterns directed by a synthetic reaction-diffusion circuit
articles_hidden.authors: Fuqing Wu, Changhan He, Samat Bayakhmetov, Duane Harris, Xin Fang, Javier Baez, Steven Ohnmacht, Qi Zhang, Xingwen Chen, Kyle R. Allison, Yang Kuang, Xiao Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Reaction-diffusion (RD) has long been proposed as a mechanism underlying biological pattern formation. However, quantitative frameworks linking circuit design to spatial organization remain limited. Here, we engineered a synthetic gene circuit, MINPAC, that couples gene expression regulation (reaction) with bacterial colony expansion and quorum sensing (diffusion) to guide bacterial cells to self-organize into periodic volumetric patterns across multiple scales, from single cells to three-dimensional colonies. The patterns exhibit robustness against environmental variations and size-dependent complexity. Mathematical modeling supports a clock-and-wavefront mechanism, where oscillatory gene expression interacts with outward expanding diffusions to generate these periodic spatial structures. Topological analysis reveals that specific network architecture is essential for pattern formation. Guided by model predictions, we further show that pattern complexity can be systematically tuned by gene dosage, with lower expression levels favoring multiple rings through faster dynamics. This work establishes a framework uniting circuit engineering and mathematical analysis for programming multicellular self-organization through RD mechanisms, with potential applications in regenerative medicine and biomaterials.

articles_hidden.title: Enzymatic degradation of a polyester-based thermoset composite resin by an engineered cutinase from Fusarium solani
articles_hidden.authors: Mikel Dolz, Matheo Berthet, Beatrice Mongili, Nuria Velasco, Alain Garillot, Julio Vidal-Navarro, Javier Viña-Gonzalez, Miguel Alcalde
articles_hidden.abstract: Thermoset composites have become indispensable high-performance materials across key industrial sectors. However, existing recycling methods have yet to deliver sustainable end-of-life solutions for these materials. Here, we report the engineering of a highly active and stable biocatalyst capable of depolymerizing polyester-based thermoset composites. First, a second-generation polyester resin was designed to enhance susceptibility to enzymatic attack. Cutinase from Fusarium solani was selected and subsequently engineered through a combination of directed evolution and computational design using two soluble surrogate motifs representative of the redesigned resin structure. The resulting variant, which incorporated 19 mutations, exhibited a 22-fold increase in activity and an 11°C improvement in melting temperature while achieving recombinant production titers at the gram-per-liter scale in yeast cultivated in fed-batch bioreactor. This engineered enzyme depolymerized the polyester resin with a total release of 6 mM (∼1.08 grams per liter) monomethyl phthalate. Together, to our knowledge, these findings constitute the first documented example of enzymatic degradation of a complex polyester resin from thermoset composite materials.

articles_hidden.title: Roseburia intestinalis counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis
articles_hidden.authors: Liangju Liu, Tiantian Gan, Liu Yang, Zhiwei Wang, Xiaowang Lv, Xiaoyan Wang, Ka Zhang, Hao Kan, Mengru Gao, Lilong Pan, Aiqin Mao, Tingting Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut Roseburia intestinalis abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E −/− ( ApoE −/− ) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element–binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain–containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral R. intestinalis supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.

articles_hidden.title: Solubility-driven morphological decoupling enables elastic electron-deficient semiconducting polymers for fully stretchable electronics
articles_hidden.authors: Hayeong Park, Qian Liu, Wenhao Li, Minji Chung, Gunmo Koo, Chien-Chung Shih, Christopher R. McNeill, Dongsheng Yan, Yang Wang, Shanshan Zhou, Mandar M. Shirolkar, Ruicheng Li, Aung Ko Ko Kyaw, Yunqi Liu, Prashant Sonar, Joon Hak Oh
articles_hidden.abstract: The development of fully stretchable electronics is limited by the scarcity of electron-deficient polymers that combine high electron mobility with mechanical elasticity. Here, we report a solubility-driven morphological decoupling strategy that mitigates this trade-off by incorporating ∼10% planar, insoluble PyF units into a semicrystalline PySe backbone. This approach yields a hierarchical morphology characterized by suppressed long-range crystallinity alongside robust local aggregation. Driven by strong fluorine (F)-sulfur (S) interactions, highly ordered face-on domains function as robust physical anchors, providing the polymer network with exceptional elasticity to reversibly dissipate stress and preserve charge percolation pathways. Consequently, the resulting terpolymer largely relieves the long-standing trade-off between charge transport and mechanical stretchability, delivering a near-unity initial electron mobility (∼1.0 square centimeter per volt per second) and retaining 0.5 square centimeters per volt per second even under 100% applied strain, representing the highest performance reported to date. To demonstrate the practical utility of this system, we fabricated stretchable ambipolar inverters and phototransistors that maintain high performance under severe deformation. Notably, the phototransistors sustain an exceptional responsivity of 15.8 amperes per watt and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 2900% at 100% strain. These results establish a powerful blueprint for intrinsically elastic semiconductors, enabling the realization of high-performance, fully deformable optoelectronic systems.

articles_hidden.title: Evolution of MEIS transcription factor activity during metazoan neural development—born to be wild
articles_hidden.authors: Pavel Fedarenchik, Hanna Polevoy, Yael Volovik, Emil Aamar, Mohammed Mahroum, Gilad Barshad, Adi Salzberg, Dale Frank
articles_hidden.abstract: Meis TALE-class proteins pattern vertebrate neural tissue, inducing hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus laevis embryos. Meis orthologs have two conserved regions: (i) Meis-specific domain and (ii) Meis-specific TALE homeodomain. Meis homeodomain proteins are present in “ancient” metazoans-eucaryotes like cnidarians, placozoans, and protozoans. We asked: When during metazoan evolution did Meis proteins acquire functionality to induce neural pattern? Using structure-function analysis in Xenopus , we show that the Meis-specific and Meis homeodomains suffice to induce the spinal cord but not the hindbrain. Meis proteins share a functionally conserved carboxyl-terminal transcription activation domain inducing the hindbrain. Ancient Meis proteins from Trichoplax and chlorophyte algae have a conserved Meis homeodomain, but lack the Meis-specific domain. Unexpectedly, these ancestral proteins robustly induce hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus , unlike metazoan proteins requiring the Meis-specific domain. Thus, in early eukaryotes, Meis prototypes were “born to be wild,” having the intrinsic capacity to induce vertebrate structures like hindbrain and neural crest, despite predating them.

articles_hidden.title: SeqA-mediated sister loci cohesion regulates the efficiency and fidelity of DNA double-strand break repair across the E. coli genome
articles_hidden.authors: Deepak K. Singh, Amir Faraz, Nuha A. Khan, Jebin Babu, T. Sabari Sankar, David Bates, Mohan C. Joshi
articles_hidden.abstract: In Escherichia coli , SeqA-mediated cohesion at snap loci on the right replichore persists longer, but its role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair remains untested. Here, we show that site-specific DSBs at snap loci confer higher cell survival than nonsnap loci. With perturbations affecting sister cohesion [Δ seqA , topoisomerase IV overexpression (T4-OE)], this survival advantage was progressively reduced, with the combined Δ seqA T4-OE strain retaining only a transient advantage. The increased survival correlates with faster repair, reflected by rapid restoration of locus copy number and shorter-lived, thinner RecA–green fluorescent protein filaments. Consistent with more accurate repair, snap loci exhibited lower mutation accumulation under normal and antibiotic stress conditions. Comparative genome analysis of E. coli strains revealed higher GATC motif counts and higher sequence conservation. Together, these findings suggest that the chromosomal organization associated with prolonged sister cohesion at snap loci promotes efficient homologous recombination–mediated DSB repair and contributes to genome conservation.

articles_hidden.title: TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Wenhao Li, Niannian Wang, Dania El Abyad, Seray Anak, Raju Kumar, Iris Ginés, Upkar Gill, Gillian Hood, James Brindley, Charles Mein, James Boot, Una Rose Wilcox, Neil Dufton, Robert Goldin, Tania Roskams, John Loy, Kalpana Devalia, Humza Malik, Adam Goralcyzk, Maria Jimenez-Ramos, Timothy J. Kendall, Jonathan A. Fallowfield, Maria Ines Castanho Martins, Krista Rombouts, Michele Vacca, Olivier Govaere, William Alazawi
articles_hidden.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo models. Hepatic TLR5 expression, but not TLR2 or TLR4, is associated with liver fibrosis and mortality. Plasma levels of TLR5’s cognate ligand flagellin are increased in MASH with advanced fibrosis and fall with liver disease improvement. Mechanistically, we identify two parallel TLR5-mediated routes to hepatocyte injury: one elicited by flagellin and the other indirectly by lipid injury. Furthermore, hepatocyte TLR5 inhibition abrogates paracrine activation of hepatic stellate cells to suppress collagen production. This is also seen ex vivo in patient-derived precision-cut liver slices where TLR5 inhibition significantly reduces lipid-induced collagen deposition. These findings reveal a new role for TLR5 signaling, specifically in the development of advanced MASH fibrosis and may offer a novel disease-specific therapeutic approach.

articles_hidden.title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory
articles_hidden.authors: David Breitbach, Moritz Bechberger, Hanadi Mortada, Björn Heinz, Roman Verba, Qi Wang, Carsten Dubs, Mario Carpentieri, Giovanni Finocchio, Davi Rodrigues, Alexandre Abbass Hamadeh, Philipp Pirro
articles_hidden.abstract: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency shift to realize nonlinear activation. Using Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, we uncover a transient neuron response with tunable fading memory: A 25% change in pump power results in a three-order-of-magnitude tuning in memory time, which we harness, demonstrating temporal integration of up to 50 magnon pulses. Last, we realize neuron triggering in a cascade of three neurons, highlighting its potential for connected magnonic circuits.

articles_hidden.title: Targeting METTL3 protects against acetaminophen-induced liver injury through HAPTOGLOBIN/CD163 macrophage axis
articles_hidden.authors: Huaxin Chen, Silin Tu, Bo Cui, Zhancheng Zeng, Xuanyong Chen, Shuai Dong, Yanli Li, Shanshan Yu, Xiao Liu, Ruiqi Xiao, Jing Guo, Xiaoqi Liang, Lijie Pan, Jiajie Chu, Yiju Huang, Chang Liu, Guo Lv, Yiwang Zhang, Wenjie Chen, Qi Zhang, Yan Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), with limited treatment options. N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is the most abundant internal epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotic RNAs and is involved in various physiological and pathological processes, serving as a potential therapeutic target for many diseases. However, little is known about the role of m 6 A in DILI. Here, we found that intrahepatic expression of Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the core catalytic subunit of RNA m 6 A methyltransferase complex, was elevated in patients with DILI and mouse DILI models. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of METTL3, achieved via either Alb-Cre ERT2 –driven recombination or adeno-associated virus (AAV)–mediated delivery of Cre, significantly protected from APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in both male and female mice. Mechanistically, hepatic METTL3 deficiency reduced m 6 A deposition on acute-phase protein haptoglobin ( Hp ) transcripts and promoted Hp transcription and translation in hepatocytes. Increased HP secreted by hepatocytes bound to its receptor CD163, expressed explicitly on macrophages, and induced highly phagocytic and anti-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, finally reducing APAP-induced hepatic injury. Moreover, two different METTL3 inhibitors, JNJ64619178 and STM2457, effectively alleviated APAP-induced liver injury. Our study thus demonstrated that hepatic inhibition of METTL3 protected against APAP-induced liver injury by promoting the cross-talk between hepatocytes and macrophages through HP/CD163, underscoring the potential of targeting METTL3 as a promising therapy for APAP overdose.

articles_hidden.title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Hanjia Zheng, Fatima Shafique, Alexander S. Qian, Mayank Garg, Florian Gessler, Jonathan L’Heureux Hache, Quan M. Quach, Bernardo L. Trigatti, Mahla Poudineh, Leyla Soleymani
articles_hidden.abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

articles_hidden.title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
articles_hidden.authors: Ines C. Osma-Garcia, Trang-My M. Nguyen, Orlane Maloudi, Mailys Mouysset, Dunja Capitan-Sobrino, Yann Aubert, Manuel D. Diaz-Muñoz
articles_hidden.abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

articles_hidden.title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
articles_hidden.authors: Wenjie Wang, Jiaxin Guo, Hong Han, Dan Yuan, Junfeng Shi
articles_hidden.abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY p HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY p HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY p HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

articles_hidden.title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
articles_hidden.authors: Xinyue Cao, Ruisi He, Zhuhao Wu, Yuanjin Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

articles_hidden.title: Phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization enables record NIR-II-to-visible-light photon upconversion
articles_hidden.authors: Kin Ting Chang, Pui Ying Wong, Shaokuan Gong, Aleksandr A. Sergeev, Kai Kin Li, Kam Sing Wong, Xihan Chen, Haipeng Lu
articles_hidden.abstract: Near-infrared-to-visible triplet−triplet annihilation photon upconversion (TTA-UC) enables harvesting low-energy photons; however, extending nanocrystal-sensitized TTA-UC into the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) remains challenging because triplet sensitization is thermodynamically disfavored under sub-triplet excitation. Here, we demonstrate that lead-free AgBiS 2 nanocrystals facilitate phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization, enabling efficient NIR-II-to-visible upconversion. Under the sub-bandgap single-photon excitation, AgBiS 2 nanocrystals exhibit anti-Stokes photoluminescence, suggesting strong exciton−phonon coupling mediated by surface states. When coupled with 5-tetracene carboxylic acid transmitters and rubrene annihilators, AgBiS 2 achieves 980 nm-to-visible upconversion with a record quantum yield of 6.22% (normalized to 100%) and an anti-Stokes shift of 0.95 eV. Time-resolved photoluminescence and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy support a surface-state-mediated uphill energy-transfer pathway coupled to low-frequency vibrational modes. Our work establishes phonon-assisted triplet sensitization as a strategy to overcome the NIR-II red wall for lead-free photon upconversion.

articles_hidden.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) binds talin and is anchored at the postsynaptic density by direct PDZ interactions
articles_hidden.authors: Yasumi Otani, Emily Goodall, Vignesh Srinivasan, Neil J. Ball, Samuel F. H. Barnett, Youlim Hwang, Dominic P. Byrne, Tobias Zech, Juha Saarikangas, Benjamin T. Goult
articles_hidden.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) is a serine/threonine kinase essential for brain development and function. Mutations in CDKL5 cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy associated with impaired synapse formation and function. However, how CDKL5 mutations disrupt synaptic function remains unclear. Here, we show that the major neuronal isoform of CDKL5 contains a C-terminal PDZ domain–binding motif that mediates direct binding to PSD-95 and SHANK PDZ domains and recruits CDKL5 to the postsynaptic density. Disrupting this motif mislocalized CDKL5, reduced dendritic spine density, and impaired spine maturation. We also show that the CDKL5 kinase domain binds the R8 rod domain of the mechanosensitive scaffold talin. Mutation of the talin-binding interface or reduced cellular contractility altered CDKL5 positioning relative to focal adhesions. These findings define how CDKL5 is targeted to synapses, suggest that talin mechanoswitching may position CDKL5 kinase activity, and highlight the importance of C-terminal anchoring for interpreting pathogenic truncations.

articles_hidden.title: Anisotropic field suppression of charge order reveals orbital-selective Kondo hybridization in UTe 2
articles_hidden.authors: Nileema Sharma, Fangjun Cheng, Hyeok-Jun Yang, Matthew Toole, James McKenzie, Mitchell M. Bordelon, Sean M. Thomas, Priscila F. S. Rosa, Yi-Ting Hsu, Xiaolong Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: UTe 2 is a rare correlated quantum material where unconventional density-wave orders, Kondo physics, spin-triplet pairing, and reentrant superconductivity coexist. Because superconductivity emerges from a strongly correlated normal state, identifying and controlling intertwined normal-state orders are essential for understanding the electronic landscape where superconductivity arises. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy in a vector magnetic field, we uncover a staggered charge density wave (CDW) in high-quality UTe 2 crystals. This CDW exhibits a strong directional field response: It is completely quenched by a modest 1.7-tesla magnetic field along the quasi–one-dimensional uranium-chain direction while remaining robust against fields along other crystallographic axes. This anisotropy suggests an orbital-driven field-tuned quantum phase transition. Unexpectedly, the same field orientation concurrently suppresses the 5f Kondo resonance. Modeling indicates a switch in the dominant hybridization channel from Te 5 p- U 5 f to U 6 d- U 5 f coupling, suggesting an intimate interplay between CDW and the Kondo effect.

articles_hidden.title: LONP-1 deficiency causes dysregulated protein synthesis within mitochondria that is suppressed by mitoribosomal mutations
articles_hidden.authors: Levi D. Ali, Avijit Mallick, Yunguang Du, Rui Li, Lihua J. Zhu, Kuang Shen, Cole M. Haynes
articles_hidden.abstract: Mitochondrial homeostasis is maintained by molecular chaperones and proteases located within the organelle. The mitochondrial matrix-localized protease LONP-1 degrades oxidatively damaged or misfolded proteins. Importantly, LONP-1 also regulates mitochondrial DNA replication. Here, we show that mutations in C. elegans that impair LONP-1 function cause dysregulation of mitochondrial DNA replication, mitochondrial RNA transcription and protein synthesis within the mitochondrial matrix. LONP-1 deficient worms had reduced levels of oxidative phosphorylation proteins despite increased mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis. Via a forward genetic screen, we identified three mutations that restored mitochondrial function and the rate of development in lonp-1 mutants to levels comparable to those in wildtype worms. Interestingly, all three suppressor mutations were found in genes encoding mitochondrial ribosome proteins. A point mutation in the mitochondrial ribosome protein MRPS-38 restored oxidative phosphorylation in lonp-1 mutant worms. Combined, our results suggest that LONP-1 regulates mitochondrial translation and that suppressor mutations within mrps-38 or mrps-15 can enhance oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly when LONP-1 function is diminished.

articles_hidden.title: Denoised vibrometry reveals noncanonical filtering at the apex of the cochlea
articles_hidden.authors: George W. S. Burwood, Pierre Hakizimana, Karl Grosh, Wajiha Zaidi, Ruikang K. Wang, Alfred L. Nuttall, Anders Fridberger
articles_hidden.abstract: How do mammals distinguish sounds with different pitch? Prevailing theory states that each position along the cochlear spiral responds best to one single stimulus frequency, forming a frequency-to-place (tonotopic) map that is preserved throughout the auditory pathways. Whether this holds in the low-frequency cochlear apex, a region important for vocal communication but technically challenging to study, is unknown. Using a differential noise-canceling technique, we recorded sound-evoked motion near the lower limit of hearing. Apical locations often had two best frequencies, contradicting the assumption of one-to-one frequency-to-place mapping. Spatially distant regions responded similarly, and brief sounds evoked synchronized motion across large distances, revealing an unusual energy propagation mode. Morphology and mathematical analyses corroborate these findings, showing that tonotopy breaks down at the apex of the cochlea. These results have important implications for cochlear implants, which currently assume tonotopic organization throughout the cochlea.

articles_hidden.title: Interfacing ultrafast single-photon-level fields with an atomic ensemble
articles_hidden.authors: Kai Shinbrough, Tegan Loveridge, Benjamin D. Hunt, Sehyun Park, Kathleen Oolman, Thomas O. Reboli, J. Gary Eden, Virginia O. Lorenz
articles_hidden.abstract: Ultrafast photons—with pulse durations on the order of 100 femtoseconds—are typical of high-rate, high-purity, entangled photon-pair sources. Efficient, coherent mapping between these states and matter-based quantum systems is an important problem in quantum optics and could enable applications in quantum frequency conversion, bandwidth conversion, and local quantum information processing at gigahertz speeds. This coherent mapping is also the initial storage step in matter-based photonic quantum memory, which can enhance multiphoton rates and allow for synchronization in quantum repeaters. Here, we use a collisionally broadened neutral atomic barium ensemble to demonstrate a quantum-compatible light-matter interface with storage efficiency of 95.6 ± 0.3%, total internal efficiency of 31 ± 1%, and noise contributions of <10 −4 photons per pulse. Using the simultaneous efficiency, bandwidth, and noise performance of this interface, we perform a full amplitude and phase reconstruction via spectral interferometry of single-photon-level fields retrieved from the interface.

articles_hidden.title: Geophysics-informed hydrologic modeling reveals contrasting regolith and bedrock responses of headwater catchments to warming
articles_hidden.authors: Chen Xiong, Hang Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Predicting how warming reshapes headwater streamflow requires distinguishing shallow and deep subsurface contributions, which remain difficult to constrain in catchment-scale models. We use seismic P-wave velocity to partition the critical zone into regolith and fractured bedrock domains within a three-dimensional physically based model and develop a particle-based attribution method to quantify their streamflow contributions and source-water ages across realizations spanning diverse hydraulic configurations. Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

articles_hidden.title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
articles_hidden.authors: Kyunghyun Jo, Yeji Kim, Yeonzu Son, Joonhee Won, Woojin Jeon, Joonhyung Kwon, Hyung Jin Choi, Young-Gyun Park, Jong-Seok Kim, Seongjun Park
articles_hidden.abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

articles_hidden.title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
articles_hidden.authors: Shiting Wang, Qiheng Qian, Yuting Liu, Yang Ding, Dechang Yang, Xing Zheng, Sijin Cheng, Guoquan Huang, Ge Gao, Jingfa Xiao, Zhang Zhang, Shuai Jiang
articles_hidden.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

articles_hidden.title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
articles_hidden.authors: Jérémie Ginzburg, Clarisse Gotti, Émilie Cloutier Debaque, Arthur Borderie, Benjamin Morillon, Laurence Martineau, Paule Lessard Bonaventure, Robert J Zatorre, Philippe Albouy
articles_hidden.abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

articles_hidden.title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
articles_hidden.authors: Xinjian Xie, Guangrui Ju, Xiongwei Luo, Shengwei Feng, Hongjiao Li, Yijun Zhang, Wenqian Feng
articles_hidden.abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

articles_hidden.title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
articles_hidden.authors: Jiayuan Zhu, Helen Forgham, Yu Qin, Xiaodi Li, Xueguang Lu, Sui Wang, David S. Ziegler, Maria Kavallaris, Thomas P. Davis, Ruirui Qiao
articles_hidden.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

articles_hidden.title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Jingchao Wang, Daoyuan Huang, Bo Liu, Weiwei Jiang, Fabin Dang, Li Chen, Tao Hou, Peiqiang Yan, Yihang Qi, Hiroyuki Inuzuka, Lei Li, Wenyi Wei
articles_hidden.abstract: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

articles_hidden.title: Reconciling the medical relevance of mitochondrial transplantation in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Eaman Abay, Joan Sanchez-Gurmaches, Jeffery D. Molkentin
articles_hidden.abstract: Mitochondria transplantation is a proposed therapeutic approach to improve the function of diseased or injured tissue. It has garnered attention and sparked debate.

articles_hidden.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
articles_hidden.authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo, Zhihao Li, Zirui Li, Tengyu Ma, Ying Tang, Zhe Li, Weiwei Zuo, Jorge Pascual, Bo Hou, Feng Yang, Xiaoli Pan, Yu Wang, Luyao Wang, Lin-Long Deng, Guixiang Li, Luca Sapienza, Antonio Abate, Meng Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl − induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles_hidden.title: Asymmetric interactions and feast-famine cycles drive chaos in microbial populations
articles_hidden.authors: William F. McLaughlin, Thomas Beardsley, Natalia L. Komarova, Megan G. Behringer
articles_hidden.abstract: Predicting the dynamics of ecological systems is a central challenge in biology. One factor that may limit predictability is ecological chaos. Theory has long suggested that even simple interactions can produce chaos, yet empirical demonstrations in living systems remain scarce. In a two-strain system of Escherichia coli , increasing the duration between resource replenishment reveals transitions from competitive exclusion to chaos, driven by asymmetric ecological interactions and periodic environmental forcing. Guided by these observations, we developed a dynamical systems framework grounded in empirical data that recapitulate the observed dynamics and predicts intermediate ecological states and transitions. Experimental validation of these predictions by implementing the corresponding conditions successfully reproduces the full range of predicted dynamical regimes. Because feast-famine cycles and asymmetric interactions are widespread in nature, our findings provide a model for uncovering the ecological and evolutionary significance of chaos, opening avenues to use resource fluctuation and interaction strength to quantify, monitor, and manipulate complex ecosystem behavior previously interpreted as stochasticity.

articles_hidden.title: Structure and dynamics of the cellular belt driving bacterial gliding motility
articles_hidden.authors: Hanxiong Liu, Yaëlle Aouizerate, Xiangan Liu, Zihe Zhang, Caterina Comas Hervada, Yongtao Zhu, Maxence S. Vincent, Eric Cascales, Bo Hu, Thierry Doan
articles_hidden.abstract: Various bacteria move on solid surfaces through a process known as gliding motility. Gliding bacteria of the phylum Bacteroidota are major ecological players in a wide variety of niches, as commensals or as pathogens. They use the type IX secretion system (T9SS) to transport adhesins to the cell surface, which then travel in a helical pattern to propel the cell. Here, we purified the filament that drives adhesin helical movement and uncovered its structure by cryo–electron microscopy. Live imaging showed that this outer membrane–associated periplasmic belt, built from T9SS core components, is powered by T9SS molecular motors. This structure functions as a moving walkway that conveys outer membrane β barrel protein–adhesin complexes, therefore coupling motor activity to directional surface translation. This study reveals a unique machinery coupling protein secretion with rapid directed movement of membrane-embedded protein complexes.

articles_hidden.title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
articles_hidden.authors: Ute Zschieschang, Sabrina Steffens, Karla Cordero-Solano, Hagen Klauk
articles_hidden.abstract: The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10 8 and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10 −12 watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

articles_hidden.title: Predictive model for nanoparticle incorporation into crystals reveals essential role of interfacial solution structure
articles_hidden.authors: Mingyi Zhang, Kuan-Ting Liu, Dong June Jang, Victorien J. B. Bernat, Ying Xia, Dongsheng Li, Hsin-Mei Kao, Zihua Zhu, Jaehun Chun, Ulrich B. Wiesner, Lara A. Estroff, Elias Nakouzi
articles_hidden.abstract: Control of interfacial phenomena remains limited by incomplete understanding of molecular-scale solution structure at solid-liquid interfaces. We address this challenge by developing and validating a comprehensive analytical model for nanoparticle incorporation during crystallization. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) probes surface functionalized to be “particle proxies” combined with three-dimensional AFM and force spectroscopy, we measure nanoparticle-calcite crystal binding energies and kinetic barriers associated with interfacial hydration layers. These measurements, together with diffusivities, parameterize a predictive model that is corroborated using surface-functionalized fluorescent silica nanoparticles incorporated into calcite. We show that surface chemistry governs incorporation by reshaping the energy landscape, with amine groups particularly favoring incorporation. Applying this approach to nanoparticles with different topologies further supports our finding that kinetic barriers play a pivotal role in incorporation processes. This synthesis science framework links interfacial solution structure, particle dynamics, and crystallization kinetics, identifying kinetic barriers as a key design principle for engineering bioinspired nanocomposites beyond empirical approaches.

articles_hidden.title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
articles_hidden.authors: Mai Liao, Roberto J. Assef, Chao-Wei Tsai, Manuel Aravena, Román Fernández Aranda, Andrew W. Blain, Tanio Díaz-Santos, Peter Eisenhardt, Jorge González-López, Hyunsung D. Jun, Xiaofeng Li, Guodong Li, Lee R. Martin, Ana Posses, Devika Shobhana, Manuel Solimano, Daniel Stern, Andrey Vayner, Jingwen Wu, Dejene Zewdie
articles_hidden.abstract: Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) imprint gravitational signatures on the matter within their sphere of influence (SoI). Nuclear gas dynamics can hence be used to accurately measure the mass of an SMBH, yet these measurements remain elusive in the early universe. We report the first dynamical measurement of an SMBH mass at z  > 2, based on high–spatial resolution observations of the ionized-carbon 157.7-micrometer and carbon monoxide (12-11) 216.93-micrometer emission lines that resolve the SoI in an obscured quasar at z  = 4.6. The radial profile of the velocity dispersion reveals a clear Keplerian rise, requiring the presence of an ∼6 × 10 9 –solar mass SMBH. We propose that heavily obscured quasars allow such tracers to survive in the inner regions and may be ideal targets for increasing dynamical SMBH mass estimates in the early universe.

articles_hidden.title: Deep ultraviolet bound states in the continuum
articles_hidden.authors: Minsu Jeong, Jihae Lee, Sangwon Lee, Jaeyun Lim, Jihwan An, Junsuk Rho
articles_hidden.abstract: Light confinement is a key strategy for enhancing light-matter interaction, and photonic crystal (PhC) slabs have emerged as a promising resonant platform due to their high Q factors and design flexibility. However, realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) regime has remained highly challenging due to the lack of suitable materials and limitations in fabrication. In this work, we propose an etchless fabrication strategy based on electron-beam lithography and atomic layer deposition. We demonstrate a shell-type PhC slab in which a low-index photoresist core is conformally encapsulated by a high-index zirconium dioxide shell. Through angle-resolved transmittance measurements, we experimentally observe symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum in the DUV regime and achieve the highest reported Q factor among resonant modes in this spectral range. Furthermore, by comparing conventional bulk-type and shell-type PhC slabs in far-field response, we show that the shell-type structure maintains comparable performance while offering fabrication advantages. These results provide a practical route for realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the DUV and open opportunities for DUV-based molecular sensing and enhanced light-matter interaction applications.

articles_hidden.title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
articles_hidden.authors: Devika Bodas, Şevval Demirci, Olga Procenko, Marine Balcou, Lennart Baumeister, Darryl Segal, Lisa Scheunemann, Carolina Rezaval
articles_hidden.abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

articles_hidden.title: A floss-based platform for native gingival crevicular fluid analysis enables noninvasive systemic and oral health monitoring
articles_hidden.authors: Yixin Yan, Asmita Veronica, Chaoqi Wang, Yue Guo, Anwei He, Minjin Gu, Lu Zhang, Ge Han, Johnson Q. Cui, Saloni Vimal Chandwaney, Jaehyeon Cho, Xuejie Wang, Sin Yu Pau, Sang Jin Lee, Ke Deng, Shuhuai Yao, Hnin Yin Yin Nyein
articles_hidden.abstract: Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) is a serum-derived biofluid in the gingival sulcus, offering access to systemic metabolic signals and localized oral inflammation. However, its diagnostic utility remains underutilized because native submicroliter volumes cannot be analyzed without specimen pooling and reagent-mediated dilution. We overcome this barrier using a floss-based platform that enables on-demand GCF analysis during routine flossing. The device integrates a dual-fiber system exploiting shear-dependent property for efficient mobilization, liquid-bridge retention, a pyramidal microfluidic sensor stack, and real-time electrofluidic volume correction. This architecture supports multiplexed electrochemical quantification of glucose, uric acid (UA), pH, and H 2 O 2 from native GCF within minutes. In human studies, GCF glucose and UA correlated with capillary blood (glucose: r  = 0.89, UA: r  = 0.78). Site-specific pH and H 2 O 2 levels differentiated inflamed from healthy periodontal sites, correlating with probing pocket depth. By converting a daily hygiene practice into a dual tool for systemic and oral health monitoring, this platform advances comorbidity management for chronic disease populations.

articles_hidden.title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
articles_hidden.authors: Yujin Han, Hyunseok Kwon, Woo Hyuk Jung, Seung Jae Huh, Goen Lee, Dong June Ahn, Heungsoo Shin
articles_hidden.abstract: Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr 2+ –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

articles_hidden.title: Discovery of volatile- and Fe-rich melts from low-velocity zones above the mantle transition zone
articles_hidden.authors: Hui-Li Zhang, Gang Zeng, Li-Hui Chen, Zhou-Chuan Huang, Zhe Han, Jian-Qiang Liu, Xiao-Jun Wang, Jin-Hai Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: Low-velocity layers atop the mantle transition zone (MTZ) are commonly observed and predicted to comprise volatile- and iron (Fe)–rich melts, yet direct evidence from natural samples remains lacking. Nephelinites from eastern China may preserve such signatures. They contain ultradeep peridotite fragments and show anomalously low potassium (K)/uranium (U) and barium (Ba)/thorium (Th) ratios, indicating derivation from recycled crustal materials in the MTZ, with high-pressure liebermannite residues retaining K-Ba. This study investigates Wuxi nephelinites, eastern China, where seismic tomography images a slab fragment in the MTZ (high-velocity anomalies) and an overlying low-velocity layer. Volatile- and Fe-rich melt inclusions [maximum FeO T content and Cl (chlorine)/K ratio of 21.8 weight % and 0.15, respectively] are identified in these rocks, consistent with predicted compositions of low-velocity zone melts. Phlogopite in unhomogenized inclusions further confirms their volatile-rich nature. Calculated densities of these inclusions exceed that of ambient mantle, thus stabilizing melts atop the MTZ. Sustained volatile influx or melt-rock reaction reduces melt density and triggers upward melt migration, forming nephelinites, providing key petrological record verifying the geophysically detected MTZ molten layer.

articles_hidden.title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
articles_hidden.authors: John T. Fink, Matthew J. Kohn, Myla A. Negrete, Katherine E. Bemis, Melissa T. R. Hawkins, Y. Hsu, Gabriela A. Farfan
articles_hidden.abstract: A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the a -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that a -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

articles_hidden.title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
articles_hidden.authors: Lucas Albacete-Albacete, Li Jin, Nanami Sato, Marta N. Shahbazi, Simon L. Bullock
articles_hidden.abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

articles_hidden.title: THERM-D uncovers distinct neural mechanisms separating morning and evening body temperature rhythms in Drosophila
articles_hidden.authors: Tadahiro Goda, Olivia M. Lopez, Richard Ramolete, Nils Reinhard, Nick Ulle, Ayumi Fukuda, Yujiro Umezaki, Kazim Rizvi, Madison G. Aikawa, Roslyn Catiis, Victoria Z. Marquez, Richard Ngo, Nikita C. Raj, Cora Fisher, Gregory T. Bui, Jalen Lee, Charlotte Helfrich-Förster, Taishi Yoshii, Fumika N. Hamada
articles_hidden.abstract: Animal body temperature rises throughout the day and peaks in the evening, a pattern conserved across diurnal endotherms and ectotherms. However, the mechanisms driving the robust body temperature rhythms (BTRs) remain largely unclear. Here, we developed a machine learning–based platform, Temperature Homeostasis Evaluation of Rhythmicity in Model Drosophila (THERM-D), enabling continuous, high-throughput analyses of BTR. Using THERM-D, we identified robust BTR patterns reflecting flies’ morning and evening behaviors and revealed the function of CRYPTOCHROME (CRY)–negative clock neurons. About half of all clock neurons lack CRY, yet their functions are only partially understood. Gal4 drivers targeting CRY-negative neurons demonstrated that these neurons control the morning temperature rise. We further show that separate clock circuits regulate morning and evening BTRs. Thus, THERM-D elucidated the role of CRY-negative clock neurons in BTR and provides a powerful platform for uncovering mechanisms underlying circadian temperature homeostasis.

articles_hidden.title: Steering nanometric reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycle for PFAS mineralization
articles_hidden.authors: Yichuan Wang, Jianfeng Zheng, Xinchun Ye, Tianlin Zhou, Ting Li, Menghan Feng, Dahong Huang, Seunghyun Weon, Menachem Elimelech, Xiaoxiong Wang, Shuo Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), known as “forever chemicals,” have highly stable C─F bonds that render them resistant to destruction by conventional water treatment processes. Here, we developed a destructive technology that does not require external photo-, electro-, or heat energy input, relying simply on Fenton-like cycles (peroxymonosulfate activation) under nanometric spatial confinement. Unlike the ordinary activation process, confinement shielded peroxymonosulfate radicals ( S O 5 • − ) from external quenching and enabled them to remain active for reductive defluorination. Coupled with oxidative sulfate radicals ( S O 4 • − ), this process unlocked a synergistic “reduction-oxidation” destruction pathway. Specifically, the catalyst was designed by planting single-atom cobalt on MXene nanosheets, whose interlaminar confinement directed efficient PFAS mineralization via alternating α-carbon defluorination (by S O 5 • − ) and decarbonization (by S O 4 • − ). We further constructed a Fenton bed that allowed highly efficient and cost-effective treatment of PFASs in complex water matrices. Our findings underscore the promising potential of nanoconfinement in driving reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycles toward efficient PFAS mineralization.

articles_hidden.title: Engineering interfacial nucleation and growth for long-life, ultrahigh-rate anode-free sodium batteries
articles_hidden.authors: Chunlin Xie, Jiaming Zhang, Shengfang Liu, Junhui Lu, Peiyu Wang, Xianghui Meng, Yougen Tang, Xiaobo Ji, Haiyan Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: The practical application of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) is limited by the poor reversibility of sodium plating and stripping on current collectors. Here, we show that conventional graphite unexpectedly regulates sodium plating and stripping through a dynamic, interactive interface that enables multidimensional charge transport. This behavior arises from the combination of ultrafast mixed ion-electron transport, reversible ether solvent cointercalation, and the anisotropic flake architecture of graphite, which together promote efficient charge exchange and edge-dominant nucleation. The resulting adaptive interface forms an ultrathin, mechanically robust SEI that stabilizes sodium plating and stripping across a wide current density range (1C to 10C). Ampere hour–level anode-free pouch cells based on this design exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.3%, retain 84.9% capacity after 1100 cycles at 3C, and display exceptional safety characteristics, including minimal temperature rise at high rates and no thermal runaway during nail penetration. These results establish a platform for controlling interfacial metal nucleation and growth in AFSBs.

articles_hidden.title: Cortical population codes for embedding sensory inputs into the prior context
articles_hidden.authors: Iacopo Hachen, Sebastian Reinartz, Alisea Stroligo, Alejandro Pequeno-Zurro, Mathew E. Diamond
articles_hidden.abstract: According to theories of the brain as a predictive network, perceptual decisions result from integrating incoming sensory inputs with prior experience. A neuronal population implementing this form of computation must not only retain information about past events but also combine this information with current sensory evidence. To examine how this integration occurs, we recorded extracellular activity from both primary sensory cortex and a target frontal region in rats performing stimulus categorization. Psychophysical analysis showed that judgments were history dependent. Sensory cortex represented the current stimulus largely independently of prior stimuli and failed to account for the history dependence seen in behavior. In contrast, frontal cortex embedded current input within a representation of prior sensory information, with the two variables aligned along partially overlapping coding dimensions. This mechanism predicted choice bias in the behavioral data and involved a disproportionate contribution from putative fast-spiking units. These findings suggest distinct contributions of sensory and frontal cortical regions to predictive processing and point to frontal cortex as a potential site where sensory history may be integrated with incoming evidence to influence perceptual decisions.

articles_hidden.title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma
articles_hidden.authors: Maya Arnould, Jean-Baptiste Assie, Clément Meiller, Ruth Sequeiros, Sandrine Imbeaud, Amélie Roehrig, Camille Boano, Delphine Le Corre, Sophie Mouillet-Richard, Lucie Poupel, Julien Lavergne, Véronique Hofman, Paul Hofman, Sarah Humez, Arnaud Scherpereel, Françoise Le Pimpec-Barthes, Jessica Zucman-Rossi, Christophe Blanquart, Marie-Claude Jaurand, Sylvie Lantuejoul, Theo Z. Hirsch, Diane Damotte, Didier Jean
articles_hidden.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

articles_hidden.title: The interferon-gamma response pathway is a targetable driver of FSHD muscular dystrophy progression
articles_hidden.authors: Beatrice Biferali, Federica Del Prete, Mara Salomè, Jose Manuel Garcia Manteiga, Reza Alemohammad, Miriam Mombellardo, Maria Pannese, Emanuele Mocciaro, Francesca Torri, İlker Eren, Elisabetta Ferraro, Dicle Ballikaya, Beatrice Ciurli, Arianna Votta, Daniele Campolungo, Daniel C. Turner, Monica Canepari, Roberto Bottinelli, Gabriele Siciliano, Serpil Eraslan, Giulia Ricci, Davide Gabellini
articles_hidden.abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is a leading neuromuscular disorder caused by the aberrant expression of the transcription factor double homeobox 4 (DUX4) in skeletal muscle. While DUX4 is normally restricted to early embryonic development, its reactivation in FSHD triggers chronic inflammation and progressive muscle degeneration. However, the precise molecular links between DUX4 and persistent immune activation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that DUX4 induces a viral mimicry-like pathway that is fundamentally uncoupled from canonical type I interferon (IFN) activation. Instead, DUX4 establishes a non-canonical innate immune state dominated by IFN-γ signaling, providing a mechanistic explanation for the non-resolving inflammation characteristic of the disease. We demonstrate that while IFN-γ treatment alone is sufficient to recapitulate key DUX4 pathogenic effects, its inhibition rescues muscle inflammation and halts disease progression in FSHD models. These findings define a “skewed viral mimicry” process driven by a disease-specific transcription factor and identify IFN-γ as a primary therapeutic target for tissue-informed immunomodulation in muscular dystrophy.

articles_hidden.title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
