articles_hidden.authors: Janni Harju, Mattia Ubertini, Deepthi Kailash, Po-Ta Chen, Pierre Ronceray, Luca Giorgetti, Thomas Gregor, David B. Brückner
articles_hidden.abstract: From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from Drosophila embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

articles_hidden.title: Light-guided photophosphorylation nanorobot rescues injured cardiomyocytes via in situ bioenergetic restoration
articles_hidden.authors: Tingting Yue, Meng Mao, Xiankun Lin, Yang Huang, Qiang He
articles_hidden.abstract: Myocardial injury is a leading cause of death worldwide and is accompanied by profound mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction in impaired cardiomyocytes. Restoring cellular bioenergetic homeostasis could be a promising strategy to promote cardiac repair; however, current clinical adenosine triphosphate (ATP) injection therapies yield limited efficacy due to the inability to achieve in situ, targeted delivery. Here, we develop a photoactivated phosphorylation nanorobot engineered to rescue impaired metabolism via targeted, in situ ATP synthesis within cardiomyocytes. These Janus photophosphorylation nanorobots are fabricated through mechanical extrusion–assisted phase separation, enabling the asymmetric integration of chromatophore-coupled F o F l -ATPases. Under structured near-infrared irradiation, the nanorobots exhibit synergistic F o F l -ATPase rotation, which simultaneously drives active propulsion and high-yield ATP catalysis. Following targeted internalization and efficient lysosomal escape, the nanorobots achieve deep penetration into injured myocardial tissue. Intracellularly, the localized elevation of ATP rebalances the NAD + /NADH ratio, suppresses pathological mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, and mitigates calcium ion overload—collectively restoring mitochondrial integrity and promoting functional myocardial recovery. This self-propelled, bioenergy-restoring nanoplatform represents a rationally designed strategy for targeted therapy of energy-deficient cardiomyopathies.

articles_hidden.title: Somatostatin 6, a master maternal mRNA driving early development
articles_hidden.authors: Jie Chen, Jing Gao, Ting Nie, Lu Liu, Huiming Yuan, Rute S. T. Martins, Adelino V. M. Canario
articles_hidden.abstract: Vertebrate genomes contain six somatostatin (SST) gene family members, of which only SST1 and cortistatin (CORT or SST2) are present in mammalian genomes. These genes encode peptides that predominantly exert inhibitory effects on growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the immune system. However, their roles in nonmammalian vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we examined zebrafish sst6 ( sst6.2 ) loss of function and discovered that maternally inherited sst6 mRNA is vital for embryonic cleavage and gastrulation. Its absence impaired calcium release from stores, calcium wave propagation, F-actin assembly, furrow ingression, and overall embryonic development. Moreover, maternal sst6 mRNA is crucial for degrading maternal mRNAs, for calcium-dependent phosphorylation of Stat3 and Smad1/5, and for activating zygotic gene transcription, including pou5f1 , nanog , and sox2 , as well as downstream pluripotency factors. This suggests that maternal sst6 mRNA acts as a master regulator of early development, a function likely conserved in other vertebrates.

articles_hidden.title: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
articles_hidden.authors: Rhian Evans, Ben P. Harvey, Bayden D. Russell
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Simulations suggested that winter MHWs could generally benefit growth, while summer MHWs produced generally negative impacts, especially at higher latitudes where species experience summer growth periods. When combined, winter and summer MHW scenarios indicated a cumulative negative effect for most species. Vulnerability was highest at the warm- and cold-range edges of species’ distributions. These simulations suggest that temperature-dependent growth may be closely linked to the seasonal timing and frequency of extreme events, with multi-season MHWs posing potential challenges for mariculture species in the future. Our simulations highlight the importance of considering multi-season impacts in climate adaptation strategies.

articles_hidden.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
articles_hidden.authors: Federico Presutti, Logan G. Wright, Shi-Yuan Ma, Tianyu Wang, Benjamin K. Malia, Tatsuhiro Onodera, Peter L. McMahon
articles_hidden.abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

articles_hidden.title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
articles_hidden.authors: Jinlei Peng, Hui Wang, Zheng Li, Jiayi Xu, Zongyan Du, Nan Cheng, Wei Li, Yadong Na, Dahai Hou, Yunzhu Xu, Xianli Yang, Yuyan Tan, Dongdong Sun, Haibo Cheng, Weiwei Tao
articles_hidden.abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

articles_hidden.title: Unblockable communication with gravity
articles_hidden.authors: Andrew J. Groszek, Charles W. Woffinden, Michael D. Harvey, Andrew G. White, Matthew J. Davis
articles_hidden.abstract: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism. However, electromagnetic signals are readily susceptible to screening and blocking, so their availability cannot be guaranteed in adverse environments. This raises a fundamental question: Can information be transmitted through an unblockable channel? Here, we show that gravity, under physically realistic conditions, offers such a path. We propose and implement a wireless communication protocol in which a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, while a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with a gravimeter. We validate this scheme experimentally, successfully transmitting a gravitational message a distance of ≈0.7 meters through a brick wall at a rate of 1 bit per minute. These results establish gravity as a viable platform for practically unblockable communication.

articles_hidden.title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development
articles_hidden.authors: Milica Popovic, Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, Lea Isermann, Marijana Croon, Aleksandra Zecic, Jana Meisterknecht, Yasmin Alameldin, Vidyarashmi Hanehalli, Triinu Siibak, Christian Frezza, Ilka Wittig, Aleksandra Trifunovic
articles_hidden.abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine–glycine–one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

articles_hidden.title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics
articles_hidden.authors: Hao Zheng, Xu Zeng, Yao Tan, Changliu He, Cheng Tu, Haitao Deng, Yu Song, Yan Wang, Beomjoon Kim, Yuan Lin, Xiaosheng Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ capable of autonomous motion monitoring and health state awareness. We develop an interface charge field mapping model that decouples complex local wing motions, enabling dynamic three-dimensional reconstruction of wing deformation. Building on this theoretical foundation, a conformal bionic mechanoreceptor is directly grown on the wing surface via layered sensitive units. By synergistically combining physics-driven kinematic feature extraction with machine learning, the system achieves real-time fault diagnosis and closed-loop aerodynamic-loss compensation. We do not add sensors to the wing, we make the wing itself the sensory organ. This embodied self-sensing paradigm establishes a new principle for structural intelligence in bionic robotics, offering a promising path toward autonomous, self-aware, and robust miniature flying systems.

articles_hidden.title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability
articles_hidden.authors: Sumin Park, Wei Qian, Jeff Folz, Van Phuc Nguyen, N. Dayanthi Perera, Wei Zhang, Abigail T. Fahim, Yannis M. Paulus, Xueding Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)–responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H 2 O 2 concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

articles_hidden.title: The importance of organics in hydrothermal environments: A synchrotron laboratory study
articles_hidden.authors: Laura E. Jenkins, Stephen P. Thompson, Eamonn T. Connolly, Celine Beck, Sarah J. Day, Lucy K. Saunders
articles_hidden.abstract: The icy moon Enceladus has hydrothermal plumes that are of astrobiologic interest as they could provide conditions to sustain life or allow for its origin. To understand the geology of hydrothermal environments on icy moons, a carbonaceous asteroid simulant similar to the material Enceladus may have accreted from was subjected to conditions analogous to that of its seafloor. The sample environment used allowed high-resolution in situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction data to be collected during the experiment. Mineral reactions were observed as they occurred. Multiple mineral reactions had a large dependence on organic matter. Organics catalyzed the breakdown of aluminosilicates and dissolved pyrite. Melanophlogite and pyrrhotite were also formed as a result of organics being present. This study reveals that organics can have a large impact on mineral reactions and likely play an important role in the geology of hydrothermal vents on icy moons, which have an abundance of organics.

articles_hidden.title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
articles_hidden.authors: Fei Xu, Adrián Fragoso-Luna, Itai Sharon, Angelo L. Angonezi, Dania Camila Pulido Barrera, Kamaludeen Mariyath Nibrasul Haque, Cristina Tocchini, Can Eser, Hiroshi Kimura, Ohad Medalia, Peter Askjaer, Susan E. Mango
articles_hidden.abstract: Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component npp-21 /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.

articles_hidden.title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
articles_hidden.authors: Amy Y. Huang, Kelly P. Burke, Marc C. Glettig, Ryan Porter, Peter Fatouros, Jonathan M. Li, Lynn Meiger, Valeria Rosado, Shuyun Xu, Jiekun Yang, Emily Robitschek, Natalie Vokes, Cora Ricker, Giuseppe Tarantino, Jiajia Chen, Tyler J. Aprati, Yiwen He, Cassia Wang, Doris Fu, Li-Lun Ho, Kyriakitsa Galani, Gordon J. Freeman, Elizabeth I. Buchbinder, F. Stephen Hodi, Christine G. Lian, Manolis Kellis, Genevieve M. Boland, Arlene H. Sharpe, David Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 ( n  = 290), anti–CTLA-4 ( n  = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 ( n  = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

articles_hidden.title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
articles_hidden.authors: Osvaldo A. Miranda, Ximena Contreras, Florian M. Pauler, Amarbayasgalan Davaatseren, Nicole Amberg, Carmen Streicher, Ana Villalba, Yuwei Chen, Anna Heger, Corentine Marie, Bassem A. Hassan, Thomas Rülicke, Simon Hippenmeyer
articles_hidden.abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

articles_hidden.title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
articles_hidden.authors: Tomoya Nakai, Rieko Kubo, Shinji Nishimoto
articles_hidden.abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

articles_hidden.title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
articles_hidden.authors: Ravi Jada, Ying Liu, Yuxiong Liu, Heng Guo, Yin-Yuan Huang, Yixuan Wang, Md Saifur Rahman, Jack Delk, Arda Aidan Arikan, Ayse Akcan Arikan, Srikanth Singamaneni, Limei Tian
articles_hidden.abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

articles_hidden.title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
articles_hidden.authors: Tiantian Su, Shiheng Liu, Adeline E. Williams, Eric Calvo, Z. Hong Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

articles_hidden.title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
articles_hidden.authors: Yi Shen, Guangshuo Cao, Jianghong Wu, Dijun Chen, Cong Feng, Ming Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

articles_hidden.title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
articles_hidden.authors: Rui Wang, Michaela Schweizer, Kristina Ponimaskine, Christian Schulze, Christine E. Gee, Thomas G. Oertner
articles_hidden.abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

articles_hidden.title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
articles_hidden.authors: Han Yu, Elliott M. Bernard, Stefania A. Mari, Tetiana Serdiuk, Kristyna Pluhackova, Michele M. Nava, Upnishad Sharma, Matilde Lucioli, Wenhui Cheng, Jack Kuipers, Martin Fussenegger, Paola Picotti, Sebastian Hiller, Petr Broz, Daniel J. Müller
articles_hidden.abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD Nterm ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD Nterm . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD Nterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME Nterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

articles_hidden.title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
articles_hidden.authors: Jingjing Lin, Yilin Chen, Jisong Hu, Muzi Xu, Dong Liu, Jinwu Peng, Lei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.
